options.content:
Did the AI investment move delivery?

Four DORA metrics, benchmarked against the 2023 State of DevOps bands, and throughput before and after adoption. Adoption is dated from the first week AI-assisted commits reached a quarter of all commits; the green bars on each chart are the weekly assisted share, so every metric is read against how far adoption had got.

Read the trend, not a single week. Deployment and pull-request history begins in the same week adoption did, so the DORA metrics show delivery across the ramp rather than before and after it. Throughput does have earlier history and is compared both ways. Nothing here is a controlled experiment.

panels.title: Adoption, week by week
panels.description: Share of all commits with verified AI assistance, per week. The S-curve the rest of the page is read against.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CAST(DATE_SUB(DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)) DAY) AS DATETIME) AS time,
       ROUND(100*SUM(c.status='assisted')/COUNT(*),0) AS `Assisted share`
FROM whodunit_commits c
WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded')
GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: This week
panels.description: Assisted share of commits in the last 7 days — the latest point on the adoption curve, on its own so it can be quoted.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(100*SUM(c.status='assisted')/COUNT(*),0) AS value
FROM whodunit_commits c
WHERE c.committed_at > (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - 7*86400)*1000000000 AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded')

panels.title: People using it
panels.description: Contributors with at least one verified AI-assisted commit in range, against everyone who committed. Counts people, not licences.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.status='assisted' THEN c.contributor END) AS `Using AI`,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.contributor) AS `Active`
FROM whodunit_commits c
WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND c.contributor IS NOT NULL AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded')

panels.title: Four DORA metrics, benchmarked (State of DevOps 2023)
Deployment frequency — per week
panels.description: Deployments per week over the selected range. Band per DORA 2023: Elite is on demand (daily or more), High is daily to weekly, Medium weekly to monthly, Low under monthly.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CASE WHEN per_day >= 1 THEN 'Elite — on demand'
            WHEN per_day >= 1/7 THEN 'High — daily to weekly'
            WHEN per_day >= 1/30 THEN 'Medium — weekly to monthly'
            ELSE 'Low — under monthly' END AS metric,
       ROUND(per_day*7,1) AS value
FROM (SELECT COUNT(*)/GREATEST(DATEDIFF(MAX(finished_date),MIN(finished_date)),1) per_day
      FROM cicd_deployment_commits WHERE $__timeFilter(finished_date)) t

panels.title: Lead time for changes — hours
panels.description: Mean pull-request cycle time, first commit to deployed, from DevLake's PR metrics. Band per DORA 2023: Elite under a day, High under a week, Medium under a month.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CASE WHEN hrs < 24 THEN 'Elite — under a day'
            WHEN hrs < 168 THEN 'High — under a week'
            WHEN hrs < 720 THEN 'Medium — under a month'
            ELSE 'Low — over a month' END AS metric,
       ROUND(hrs,1) AS value
FROM (SELECT AVG(pr_cycle_time)/60 hrs FROM project_pr_metrics
      WHERE pr_cycle_time IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(pr_merged_date)) t

panels.title: Change failure rate
panels.description: Share of deployments that failed. Band per DORA 2023: Elite 5% or under, High 10%, Medium 15%, Low above. Counts failed deployments, not customer impact.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CASE WHEN pct <= 5 THEN 'Elite — 5% or under'
            WHEN pct <= 10 THEN 'High — 10% or under'
            WHEN pct <= 15 THEN 'Medium — 15% or under'
            ELSE 'Low — over 15%' END AS metric,
       ROUND(pct,1) AS value
FROM (SELECT 100*SUM(result='FAILURE')/COUNT(*) pct FROM cicd_deployment_commits
      WHERE $__timeFilter(finished_date)) t

panels.title: Time to restore — hours
panels.description: Mean time from incident opened to resolved. Band per DORA 2023: Elite under an hour, High under a day, Medium under a week. Rests on few incidents; moves a lot with each one.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CASE WHEN hrs < 1 THEN 'Elite — under an hour'
            WHEN hrs < 24 THEN 'High — under a day'
            WHEN hrs < 168 THEN 'Medium — under a week'
            ELSE 'Low — over a week' END AS metric,
       ROUND(hrs,1) AS value
FROM (SELECT AVG(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE,created_date,resolution_date))/60 hrs FROM incidents
      WHERE resolution_date IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(created_date)) t

panels.title: The same four, across the adoption ramp
Deployments per week
panels.description: Weekly deployments (line) against assisted share (bars). Rising together is the pattern a board wants to see; it is still a correlation.

targets.rawSql:
WITH a AS (
  SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)) DAY) w, 100*SUM(c.status='assisted')/COUNT(*) share
  FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded') GROUP BY w),
m AS (SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(finished_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(finished_date) DAY) w, COUNT(*) v FROM cicd_deployment_commits WHERE $__timeFilter(finished_date) GROUP BY w)
SELECT CAST(m.w AS DATETIME) AS time, ROUND(m.v,1) AS `Deployments`, ROUND(a.share,0) AS `Assisted share`
FROM m LEFT JOIN a ON a.w = m.w ORDER BY time

panels.title: Lead time per week
panels.description: Mean PR cycle time in hours (line) against assisted share (bars). Falling as adoption rises is the favourable pattern.

targets.rawSql:
WITH a AS (
  SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)) DAY) w, 100*SUM(c.status='assisted')/COUNT(*) share
  FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded') GROUP BY w),
m AS (SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(pr_merged_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(pr_merged_date) DAY) w, AVG(pr_cycle_time)/60 v FROM project_pr_metrics WHERE pr_cycle_time IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(pr_merged_date) GROUP BY w)
SELECT CAST(m.w AS DATETIME) AS time, ROUND(m.v,1) AS `Lead time, hours`, ROUND(a.share,0) AS `Assisted share`
FROM m LEFT JOIN a ON a.w = m.w ORDER BY time

panels.title: Change failure rate per week
panels.description: Failed share of deployments (line) against assisted share (bars). The one to watch: faster delivery that fails more has not improved.

targets.rawSql:
WITH a AS (
  SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)) DAY) w, 100*SUM(c.status='assisted')/COUNT(*) share
  FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded') GROUP BY w),
m AS (SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(finished_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(finished_date) DAY) w, 100*SUM(result='FAILURE')/COUNT(*) v FROM cicd_deployment_commits WHERE $__timeFilter(finished_date) GROUP BY w)
SELECT CAST(m.w AS DATETIME) AS time, ROUND(m.v,1) AS `Change failure %`, ROUND(a.share,0) AS `Assisted share`
FROM m LEFT JOIN a ON a.w = m.w ORDER BY time

panels.title: Time to restore per week
panels.description: Mean incident recovery in hours (line) against assisted share (bars). Weeks with no incidents are gaps, not zero.

targets.rawSql:
WITH a AS (
  SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)) DAY) w, 100*SUM(c.status='assisted')/COUNT(*) share
  FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded') GROUP BY w),
m AS (SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(created_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(created_date) DAY) w, AVG(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE,created_date,resolution_date))/60 v FROM incidents WHERE resolution_date IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(created_date) GROUP BY w)
SELECT CAST(m.w AS DATETIME) AS time, ROUND(m.v,1) AS `Recovery, hours`, ROUND(a.share,0) AS `Assisted share`
FROM m LEFT JOIN a ON a.w = m.w ORDER BY time

panels.title: Throughput per week, before and after
panels.description: Average per week on each side of the adoption date, for the three things that have history on both sides. Adoption date is derived from the data. A difference, not an effect: team size and work mix also changed.

targets.rawSql:
WITH adopt AS (
  SELECT MIN(w) AS d FROM (
    SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(committed_at/1e9)), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(FROM_UNIXTIME(committed_at/1e9)) DAY) w,
           SUM(status='assisted')/COUNT(*) share
    FROM whodunit_commits GROUP BY w HAVING share >= 0.25) t),
iss AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN i.resolution_date >= adopt.d THEN 'after' ELSE 'before' END side,
         COUNT(*)/GREATEST(COUNT(DISTINCT DATE_SUB(DATE(i.resolution_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(i.resolution_date) DAY)),1) per_week
  FROM issues i CROSS JOIN adopt
  WHERE i.status='DONE' AND i.resolution_date IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(i.resolution_date)
  GROUP BY side),
com AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9) >= adopt.d THEN 'after' ELSE 'before' END side,
         COUNT(*)/GREATEST(COUNT(DISTINCT DATE_SUB(DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)) DAY)),1) per_week
  FROM whodunit_commits c CROSS JOIN adopt
  WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded') GROUP BY side),
pr AS (
  -- project_pr_metrics rather than pull_requests: it is the table the
  -- delivery dashboard already reads for PRs, so the two agree.
  SELECT CASE WHEN p.pr_merged_date >= adopt.d THEN 'after' ELSE 'before' END side,
         COUNT(*)/GREATEST(COUNT(DISTINCT DATE_SUB(DATE(p.pr_merged_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(p.pr_merged_date) DAY)),1) per_week
  FROM project_pr_metrics p CROSS JOIN adopt
  WHERE p.pr_merged_date IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(p.pr_merged_date) GROUP BY side)
SELECT 'Issues closed / week' AS metric,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN side='before' THEN per_week END),1) AS `Before adoption`,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN side='after'  THEN per_week END),1) AS `After adoption` FROM iss
UNION ALL SELECT 'Commits / week',
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN side='before' THEN per_week END),1),
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN side='after'  THEN per_week END),1) FROM com
UNION ALL SELECT 'PRs merged / week',
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN side='before' THEN per_week END),1),
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN side='after'  THEN per_week END),1) FROM pr

panels.title: Issues closed per week
panels.description: Issues resolved each week (line) against assisted share (bars). This one has months of history before adoption, so the shape before the bars appear is the baseline.

targets.rawSql:
WITH a AS (
  SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(FROM_UNIXTIME(c.committed_at/1e9)) DAY) w, 100*SUM(c.status='assisted')/COUNT(*) share
  FROM whodunit_commits c WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded') GROUP BY w),
i AS (SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(resolution_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(resolution_date) DAY) w, COUNT(*) n FROM issues
      WHERE status='DONE' AND resolution_date IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(resolution_date) GROUP BY w)
SELECT CAST(i.w AS DATETIME) AS time, i.n AS `Issues closed`, ROUND(a.share,0) AS `Assisted share`
FROM i LEFT JOIN a ON a.w=i.w ORDER BY time

panels.title: Where lead time goes, and whether quality held
Lead time by stage, per week
panels.description: Mean hours per pull request in each stage, stacked. Coding is the stage AI touches directly; waiting for review is the one it usually does not. If the stack shrinks only in coding while review wait grows, the bottleneck moved rather than went away. A stage with no data is absent, not zero — review stages need review activity collected by DevLake.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CAST(DATE_SUB(DATE(pr_merged_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(pr_merged_date) DAY) AS DATETIME) AS time,
       ROUND(AVG(pr_coding_time)/60,1) AS `Coding`,
       ROUND(AVG(pr_pickup_time)/60,1) AS `Waiting for review`,
       ROUND(AVG(pr_review_time)/60,1) AS `In review`,
       ROUND(AVG(pr_deploy_time)/60,1) AS `To deploy`
FROM project_pr_metrics
WHERE pr_merged_date IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(pr_merged_date)
GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: Deployment outcomes per week
panels.description: Succeeded and failed deployments, stacked. The failed slice is the change failure rate in absolute terms.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CAST(DATE_SUB(DATE(finished_date), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(finished_date) DAY) AS DATETIME) AS time,
       SUM(result='SUCCESS') AS `Succeeded`, SUM(result='FAILURE') AS `Failed`
FROM cicd_deployment_commits WHERE $__timeFilter(finished_date)
GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: Rework rate, each side
panels.description: Share of commits that are fixes, assisted against unassisted. Speed that comes back as rework is not speed. A fix rate, not a defect rate.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CASE WHEN c.status='assisted' THEN 'AI-assisted' ELSE 'Unassisted' END AS metric,
       ROUND(100*SUM(c.purpose='fix')/COUNT(*),1) AS value
FROM whodunit_commits c
WHERE c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND c.status IN ('assisted','unassisted','undetermined','uninstrumented','unmatched','degraded')
  AND CASE c.status WHEN 'assisted' THEN 1 WHEN 'unassisted' THEN 1 END = 1
GROUP BY c.status HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5

options.content: What this page does not claim. A DORA metric that improved while adoption rose is a correlation on one team over a few weeks — hiring, release calendars and incident luck all move these numbers too. Change failure rate counts failed deployments, not customer impact. Mean time to recovery rests on a small number of incidents and moves a lot with each one. Time saved and cost per feature are not measured and are not shown. The cohort split behind the rework rate is self-selected.

target.rawSql:
WITH adopt AS (
  SELECT MIN(w) AS d FROM (
    SELECT DATE_SUB(DATE(FROM_UNIXTIME(committed_at/1e9)), INTERVAL WEEKDAY(FROM_UNIXTIME(committed_at/1e9)) DAY) w,
           SUM(status='assisted')/COUNT(*) share
    FROM whodunit_commits GROUP BY w HAVING share >= 0.25) t) SELECT UNIX_TIMESTAMP(d)*1000 AS time, 'AI adoption reached 25% of commits' AS text FROM adopt WHERE d IS NOT NULL
